newsitem.title: USA: Calif. unemployment rate drops, recovery strong - Gov.
newsitem.headline: Calif. unemployment rate drops, recovery strong - Gov.

text.p: California's unemployment rate dropped to 6.9 percent in November from a revised 7.0 percent in October, state officials said Friday.
The state gained about 29,700 jobs in the past month. Construction, manufacturing, mining, retail and wholesale trade and services continued to post large job gains.

The state unemployment rate is now more than a full percentage point lower than it was a year ago, and employment in the state is at an all-time record high for the third month in a row, according to California Gov. Pete Wilson.
"California's economic recovery is solid," Wilson said in a statement. "The continuing strong economic recovery is good news for all Californians."
During the next three years, California is expected to gain close to a million jobs, more than 15 percent of the projected national gain, Wilson said.

Separately, economists in the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco's Economic Letter reported Friday that a strengthening of California labor markets in 1995 and early 1996 helped stem migration out of the state.
